description: Clock divider with eight outputs whose divisions can be rotated, spread across the range, and reset on their own

params.text: Chooses whether each output pulses at the start of its division or halfway through it
Chooses the shape of the outputs: GATE holds each one high for half of its own division, TRIG gives a pulse one input clock wide
One of the two switches setting the highest division: to the left it gives 32 or 64, to the right 8 or 16, and the other switch settles which
One of the two switches setting the highest division: to the left it gives 16 or 64, to the right 8 or 32, and the other switch settles which
Turned on, the eight outputs are spaced across the whole division range rather than running one, two, three and so on
Set to 16, every count is cleared after twice the highest division has gone by, so after 16, 32, 64 or 128 clocks; OFF leaves the counts running

inputs.text: The clock being divided, read high above 2V and low below 1V
Shifts which division each output carries, 0V to 5V walking through the whole set
A rising edge above 2V sets every output's count back to the start

outputs.text: A 10V gate or trigger at this output's own division of the incoming clock, set by the rotate jack together with the two max-division switches

notes: The division printed beside an output is what it carries with nothing patched into ROTATE and SPREAD off; rotating moves every output to a different division.

inputs.0: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.1:
0 to 5V · continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.2: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
